title: Count both costs
hints: Run the first sample by hand. A value that costs 1 op per element, has 2 uses and 4 elements is computed 8 times when it is fused. Which input does `fuse_cost` never look at?
Staging writes each float to the temp once, and that is the `mem * n` already there. What does each use then have to do to get the float back?
`fuse_cost` is `ops * uses * n`. `stage_cost` is `ops * n + mem * n + mem * uses * n`. Leave `choose` as it is.

answer.explain: Fusing repeats the whole chain once per use, so its cost is `ops * uses * n`. Staging runs the chain once (`ops * n`), writes every float to the temp once (`mem * n`) and reads every float back once per use (`mem * uses * n`). Staging wins only when the arithmetic it saves, `ops * (uses - 1) * n`, is larger than the memory traffic it adds. With one use it saves nothing, and with `ops` of 0 (a plain load) there is nothing to save.
